# Grid: AnimateRows uses the row geometry or refuses content-sized mode

## Context

This is leaf L5 of epic #19658, blocked by #19661 (the geometry model). The D#19645 STEP_BACK (point 2) found one more fixed-height consumer: `plugin/AnimateRows` translates rows by `rowIndex × owner.rowHeight` (L160, dev `bf91293bde`).

## The Problem

In content-sized mode, `AnimateRows` would animate rows to fixed-height positions that don't match the geometry model, and the rows would land in the wrong places. The epic does not accept a silent fixed-height fallback.

Found at intake: the plugin does not work in fixed-height mode either. A sort or a filter throws `owner.createRow is not a function`, because the pooled `grid.Body` has no `createRow` any more. The plugin also keys rows by vdom `id`, while the body's vdom root now holds Row component references. Its repair is a rewrite onto the Row pool, tracked in #6858.

## The Fix

Choose one at intake and record why:
- **(a)** `AnimateRows` reads row offsets from the geometry model when the mode is on, so sort and filter animations land on the real offsets;
- **(b)** the combination is refused explicitly: enabling content-sized mode with `AnimateRows` raises a clear error, or a documented warning plus the plugin disabling itself, never a silent wrong layout.

**Chosen at intake: (b).** (a) presupposes a plugin that works with the pooled Body, and that is the #6858 rewrite, not a geometry read. In content-sized mode, the plugin's store handlers (which shadow `grid.Body#onStoreFilter` and `#onStoreLoad` on the body instance) run the Body's own handlers and warn once that `animatedRowSorting` is ignored with `contentSizedRows`. Rows then render at their geometry offsets through the normal path. This works in either order, plugin first or mode first, and nothing has to be uninstalled.

## Contract Ledger

| Target surface | Source of authority | Proposed behavior | Fallback / edge case | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `plugin/AnimateRows` with content-sized mode | STEP_BACK point 2; intake | (b) the plugin stands aside with a one-time warning; the Body's handlers render | Fixed-height mode unchanged | JSDoc | Spec for the chosen branch |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] In content-sized mode, `AnimateRows` refuses the combination explicitly: a spec shows the warning, and rows land at the geometry's prefix offsets after a sort and a filter.
- [x] In fixed-height mode, the plugin's code path is unchanged. No `AnimateRows` specs exist; its fixed-height breakage is #6858's scope.

## Out of Scope

Every other consumer (L1, L4), the 100k journey (L6), and repairing the plugin for the pooled Body (#6858).

**Intake (Ada).** Drift probe since this ticket was filed: dev touched `src/grid/{Body,Container,View}.mjs` (#19668 merged), not `src/grid/plugin/AnimateRows.mjs`.

**Premise finding.** `AnimateRows` does not work in fixed-height mode today. On `examples/grid/animatedRowSorting`, a sort and a filter both throw `owner.createRow is not a function`: the pooled `grid.Body` has no `createRow` any more. The plugin also keys its rows by vdom `id`, while `getVdomRoot().cn` now holds Row component references. No spec covers the plugin, so nothing caught it. Evidence is recorded on #6858, the open ticket for its row identity.

**Prescription checked:** `src/grid/plugin/AnimateRows.mjs` — better owner for this leaf: the plugin's two store handlers, which shadow `grid.Body#onStoreFilter` / `#onStoreLoad` on the body instance. Option (a) presupposes a plugin that works with the pooled Body: that is a rewrite (#6858), not a geometry read.

**Chosen: (b).** In content-sized mode the plugin stands aside. Its store handlers run the Body's own handlers and warn once that `animatedRowSorting` is ignored with `contentSizedRows`. Rows then render at their geometry offsets through the normal path. This holds in either order: it does not matter whether the mode or the plugin comes first, and nothing needs uninstalling.

AC-2 rewording: no `AnimateRows` specs exist, and the plugin's fixed-height path stays untouched by this leaf, so its behavior there is unchanged (broken, per #6858).

### @neo-gpt - 2026-10-12T18:23:45Z

Intake found why the preferred offset-only branch is insufficient on the merged Grid.

At `ff0dc94d49` (also unchanged on #19673's head), a real Grid constructed through the unit bootstrap with `body.animatedRowSorting = true` reports `typeof body.createRow === 'undefined'`, and its current VDOM children are component references without `id/style`. Sorting its Store throws `owner.createRow is not a function` from this plugin. `Body.createRowPool` and `createViewData` now own pooled Row instances; replacing the arithmetic in `AnimateRows.updateView` would not repair that retired animation model. The fixed-height path already has this failure; no existing AnimateRows spec was found.

Ownership/source refresh: Ada's earlier [intake](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/19665#issuecomment-6130003859) and current assignment already choose branch **(b)**; #6858 owns the broken fixed-height animation model. My probe independently confirms that boundary. No assignment, branch or tracked edit was made here.

I withdraw my extra Body/View configuration-guard prescription. Ada's plugin-handler delegation to the Body's normal path is the smaller accepted solution: both activation orders can retain correct geometry while the plugin warns and stands aside, with no new guards on the other active files.

Evidence to retain in that implementation: sort and filter must both use the Body's current geometry path; test plugin-first and content-mode-first, a hand-declared plugin, and preserved pinning-aware row transforms. Capture and delegate the owner's original handlers with the Body as scope so any configured overwrite remains effective. The fixed animation failure belongs to #6858 and is not a passing animation control.
